factual_notes: 1955 Court of Inquiry report: G-ALYU burst after 3,057 pressure cycles (1,221 actual and 1,836 simulated), with the test rupture at the forward escape hatch (Fig. 7; pp. 24-27). The in-service G-ALYP crack origin was a rivet hole at the rear ADF window cut-out. https://asn.flightsafety.org/reports/1954/19540408_COMT_G-ALYY.pdf

The final beat is a 2016 museum photograph of the G-ALYU fatigue-test panel, not G-ALYP accident wreckage and not a claim that this panel is the initial forward escape-hatch rupture. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Fatigue_Test_on_Fuselage_of_Comet_1_G-ALYU_(27698073420).jpg

factual_notes: Paul Hudson photographed Comet wreckage in the Alan Turing exhibition on 11 August 2012.
